newsitem.title: USA: SEC says T2 Medical executives settle charges.
newsitem.headline: SEC says T2 Medical executives settle charges.

text.p: Four former executives of a medical company agreed to pay a total $489,333 in penalities to settle charges they carried out a fraudulent accounting scheme, the Securities and Exchange Commission said Wednesday.

Joseph Allegra, 48, David Hersh, 33, J. Lee Ledbetter, 51, and H. Flynn Clyburn, 48, of the former T2 Medical Inc, neither admitted nor denied charges filed in a civil complaint by the SEC in U.S. District Court in Manhattan.

In its complaint, the agency charged that as a result of alleged fraudulent practices conducted by the four men, T2's reported net income in each of the first two quarters of fiscal year ended Sept. 30, 1993 was "materially overstated."
SEC said it also charged Ledbetter with insider trading for allegedly selling 10,000 common shares knowing that T2's financial condition was materially overstated.

At the time of the allegations, T2 was a national provider of alternate site health care services. T2 merged with three other publicly-held health care companies in July 1994 to form Coram Healthcare Corp.
